newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FINMIN TO ISSUE FIXED INTEREST SECURITIES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FINMIN TO ISSUE FIXED INTEREST SECURITIES.

text.p: Bulgaria's finance ministry considers issuing more fixed interest securities reflecting expectations of stability after a currency board launch eleven days ago, Deputy Finance Minister Plamen Oresharski said.
"At this stage we plan most of our issues to be three-six- and 12-month fixed interest government bonds," Oresharski told Reuters.
Currently the Finance Ministry sustains banks' liquidity through short-term discount treasury bills sold weekly by the ministry.

The fixed interest bonds will be more attractive for investors as drastic fluctuations in the interest rates are not expected after Bulgaria launched on July 1 an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate regime to stabilise its fragile financial system, he said.
Bulgaria's currency board system anchoring the lev to the mark, bans all forms of central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
Interest rates remain a key instrument regulating liquidity in the banking system under the currency board system through the market of government securities and interbank deposits.
Bulgarian interest rates, are expected to shadow the interest rates of the anchor currency, the mark, plus a risk premium, said Oresharski.
He saw annual interest rates slightly rising to 10 to 12 percent later this year.
"In cases of liquidity shortages the risk premium may double," he added.

Interest rates have come down to 0.58 percent monthly from 18 percent in March, reflecting stabilisation of the economy following an International Monetary Fund reform and funding deal reached in March.
"Rates fell in the past months not because of fundamental changes in the Bulgarian economy, but due to excessive lev liquidity and higher demand for long-term paper," said Oresharski.
The central bank cut the annual rate to 6.96 percent from July 14.
The ministry may consider more regular issues of longer term papers in September, said Oresharski.

"First we will see how the three-year floating coupon issue we placed this week trades, and then probably plan such issues once or twice a month," he added. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
